scope: Proposition 9.6 (Uniform barriers for straight-attachment layouts) of the manuscript “Uniform real Lipschitz surfaces on the triangular lattice” (preprints/Uniform-real-Lipschitz-surfaces-on-the-triangular-lattice-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce5ae39087f446a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 61. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix θ > 0, m < ∞, a > 0, and for mixed layouts fix κ > 0. There is p > 0 such that, for every compatible collection of at most m (θ, R)-barriers with the preceding layout, the conditional probability that all continuations of the observed strands avoid all the barriers is at least p. Pure exterior attachments are allowed when the prescribed heights are at least λ∗ > 0 on a positive attachment and at most −λ∗ on a negative attachment; p may then depend on λ∗. Interior attachment constants do not depend on it. For diverging-scale applications assume local thickness in the endpoint testing windows: after cutting the observed system by a generous square of side comparable to d, each retained component meets its rim or has diameter at least cd, and a nearby attachment component has diameter at least cd. At bounded lattice scales the compatible finite sign fences are required not to prescribe both signs on one hexagon; they are treated by insertion.
